segments.t: Configure backup retention, the encryption method and the automatic backup. Open via KTPH001Configuration → Global Settings → BackupKTPH002; stored in KTPH000.
Backups are ALWAYS encrypted. Choose one mode, ZIP with password or GPG. The chosen mode needs its credential or its GPG key; without one, the backup stops with an error before anything is written.

KTPH002Maximum Backups:KTPH003 Set to KTPH000 to keep backups indefinitely; any other value (1–100) will automatically delete the oldest backups in KTPH001 once the limit is reached, counting password ZIP and GPG backups together. When using password-based encryption, select a credential from the management system. When using GPG encryption, select an available GPG key. The encryption type is stored in the global settings and determines which credential or key ID is used for future backups.
Once a backup has been made, the tab shows KTPH000Last Backup:KTPH001 with its date, time and the path it was written to.

korTTY can write a backup on its own, into a folder you choose, as often as you choose. The automatic backup uses the same content and the same encryption as KTPH001Configuration → Create BackupKTPH002: it is always encrypted with the mode selected above, and it rotates older copies into KTPH000 under the same KTPH003Maximum number of backupsKTPH004 rule. The section header links to this page with KTPH005Open in manualKTPH006.

KTPH000WeeklyKTPH001 is the default; KTPH002DailyKTPH003 and KTPH004MonthlyKTPH005 are the alternatives, KTPH006OffKTPH007 disables the automatic backup. A month is a calendar month, so a backup written on the 31KTPH008stKTPH009 is next due at the end of the following month.

Where the backup is written, for example a folder on a network drive or in a synchronised cloud folder. Type a path or use KTPH000Browse…KTPH001. The folder must already exist: korTTY never creates it, because a path that is missing right now may be a drive that is not mounted, and a folder created in its place would silently receive every backup from then on.

Nothing runs until a folder is set, so an update to a version with this feature does not start writing files anywhere by itself. korTTY checks whether a backup is due two minutes after startup and then once an hour; the check compares the stored time of the last automatic backup (KTPH000) with the schedule, so a backup that was missed because the computer slept or korTTY was closed is written at the next check instead of waiting another interval. A manual backup does not reset the schedule.
The status line under the two fields says when the last automatic backup ran and when the next one is due, or why none can run right now:
KTPH000No folder chosen yetKTPH001, or KTPH002the folder does not exist right nowKTPH003: pick or mount the folder; korTTY retries hourly.
KTPH000No credential selectedKTPH001 / KTPH002No GPG key selectedKTPH003: the encryption mode above has nothing to encrypt with; choose one. A backup is never written unencrypted.

KTPH000Waiting for the vault to be unlockedKTPH001: KTPH002ZIP with PasswordKTPH003 decrypts the backup password with your master password, so this mode runs only while the vault is unlocked; KTPH004GPG EncryptionKTPH005 runs even with a locked vault.
KTPH000The last automatic backup failedKTPH001: the error message from the backup, also written to the application log.
When a run is skipped for one of these reasons or fails, korTTY shows one desktop notification per reason (not one per hourly check), where desktop notifications are available and allowed.

An enterprise policy can set the schedule (including KTPH001OffKTPH002) and the folder with KTPH000; the locked fields then show the "managed by your organization" hint. See KTPH003Enterprise policyKTPH004.

Backups include KTPH000, so normalized host:port trust decisions shared by interactive Terminal, SFTP, and Mosh bootstrap connections survive restore; the transient cross-process KTPH001 file is not included. JobScheduler host-key pins remain separately stored in KTPH002.

Besides these, a backup carries the connections, credentials, GPG and SSH key entries with the copied SSH key files, global settings, JobScheduler jobs, snippets and snippet analyses, AI and swarm chats, themes, environments, project workspaces and the master-password check file KTPH000, but not the auto-unlock copy of the master password. The complete list of what a backup contains and leaves out is on KTPH001Backup KTPH003 restoreKTPH002.

Local-AI backups include KTPH000, KTPH001 and KTPH002 so GGUF and MLX model registrations, role assignments, and knowledge-source definitions can be restored. They exclude GGUF weights, llama.cpp runtime packages, temporary sidecar data, source documents, and regenerable HNSW snapshots; see KTPH003Backup KTPH005 restoreKTPH004.
